statement: Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be the roots of $x^{3}+px^{2}+qx+r=0$. Prove that $\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}+\gamma^{2}=p^{2}-2q$.
solution: By Vieta, $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=-p$ and $\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha=q$. Now $(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^{2}=\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}+\gamma^{2}+2(\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha)$. Substituting gives $p^{2}=\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}+\gamma^{2}+2q$, so $\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}+\gamma^{2}=p^{2}-2q$.
hints: Write the square of the sum of the roots.
Relate the cross terms to the coefficient $q$.
